capabilityLadder.legend: DESIGNED > IMPLEMENTED > INTEGRATED (consumed on the production path) > TESTED (unit + positive control) > BENCHMARKED > VALIDATED ON OUTPUT

instrumentProfiles.note: 32 profiles; getInstrumentDefinition is an adapter over them on the production path (INTEGRATED for range / polyphony / leap / controls, as before); gestures, role suitability, blend, density tolerance and doubling have no production reader yet (B-02 composer split).

unknownInstrumentNeverAPiano.note: family 'unknown' routes to no native renderer, so an export of such a track is preview-only with the reason; partComposer.safeDefinition / musicalConstraints.safeDefinition (not B-03 files) still fall back to {0,127} / 'keys' when getInstrumentDefinition *throws* - it no longer throws, so those paths are dead, but they should read definition.profile.status and report (integration point for B-00).

registerPlanPitchBands.note: deriveOrchestrationBudget (production path) now carries registerPlan and derives registerShift / registerOccupancy from it; registerBoundsFor is a pure function the composer does not call yet (referencePartComposer.registerBounds still uses comfortableRange + the section's majority band) - B-02.

rangeAwareSoundSelection.rung: INTEGRATED + TESTED on the API side; the live worker publishes no ranges until restarted
rangeAwareSoundSelection.note: resolveTrackAsset / selectTrackSound reject an asset whose keyRange does not cover the notes (exportEngine already passes the notes); the local worker's /health gains keyRange etc. from known_asset_ranges.json once the lead restarts it; the sfizz cloud route (nativeRendererRouting) already has keyRange on its map entries but nothing checks them - integration point.

silenceAsADecision.note: shouldRest is a pure function with named conventions and a positive control per convention; B-01 supplies the arc/window fields, B-02 honours a tacet.

honestLimits: The register plan is not read by any composer yet: the owner's strings would still be written at 79-91 by referencePartComposer.registerBounds until B-02 calls registerBoundsFor. The evidence shows what the plan *would* hand the composer, not what was rendered.

The plan's numbers in this file come from the owner's *stored* section plan (export v6); re-deriving the plan from the Song Model fixture without the owner's brief yields bass + drums only (diagnosis F4: source RMS as intent), so a fixture-only run cannot reproduce the string bed. Both runs are in registerPlan.test.ts.

The stored plan still has 'keys' as LEAD everywhere and 'mix' as a family (diagnosis F5). The register plan takes the plan as given: the piano bed is the 'mix' entry; the 'keys' LEAD is planned as a line and does not own a band. B-01 fixes the plan, not this stream.

Vocal register protection is implemented but the owner's song has vocals.status = not_available, so every window here says vocal: not_available and no vocal band was protected. The synthetic test covers the detected case.

Collision rules are conventions expressed as thresholds (a fourth of overlap, a fifth between centres, 10 semitones minimum for a close voicing, 4 voices in C3-B3). They were checked against the owner's plan and four synthetic layouts, not against a corpus; no critic has been calibrated on them (B-05/B-08).

Profile numbers: GM ranges, polyphony, leaps and breath come from instrumentReference.ts (calibrated on 30,570 human windows); register character, comfortable ranges, role registers, suitability, blend, density tolerance and doubling are the orchestration references' conventions written down by this stream and reviewed by nobody independent yet. They are labelled as such (source: orchestration-reference / platform-convention).

The palette word 'strings' resolves to the violin desk (violin_section) because one track renders through one asset (the violin ensemble on both workers); the full section with violas / cellos / basses needs one track per desk, which the composer cannot write yet. A single 'strings' track therefore cannot realise the cellos 48-64 the plan proposes.

String-section polyphony in the definition is 8 (four desks divisi a2, platform convention), not the GM table's 16, and the pre-B-03 strings leap of 10 became the GM-calibrated 24: two pinned tests (playabilityRepair.test.ts, musicalConstraints.test.ts) were rewritten to derive their fixtures from the definition instead of the old numbers.

Family 'winds' and 'unknown' were added to InstrumentDefinition.family and to PERFORMANCE_CAPABILITIES in musicEngines.ts (outside the getInstrumentDefinition block) - the smallest change that keeps typecheck honest; the openapi spec carries no family enum, so generated clients are unaffected.

The percussion stem of v6 played GM 54 (tambourine) on the DRSKit, where key 54 is the left crash's tip: the new mappedKeys check would *allow* it (the key is mapped) - a mapped key is not the right sound; instrument-specific key maps for kits are not modelled.

The live worker (:8022) has not been restarted with this code: its /health still publishes no ranges, so range-aware selection on the production path is inert until the lead restarts it (no manifest change needed: known_asset_ranges.json is keyed by sfzSha256). The sfizz cloud worker's map already carries keyRange per entry; the export does not check it (integration point: exportEngine / nativeRendererRouting).
The two synths (Surge XT, Dexed) are declared 0-127 by convention; no measurement of their audible range was made.
Nothing here was rendered or listened to: no audio evidence in this PR.
integrationPoints: referencePartComposer.ts:registerBounds (B-00/B-02 owner) -> call registerBoundsFor({ profile, role, window: { startBar, endBar }, plan: request.orchestrationBudget.registerPlan, instrument }) and honour tacet / desks.

partComposer.ts:safeDefinition and musicalConstraints.ts:safeDefinition / checkArrangementConstraints -> getInstrumentDefinition no longer throws; check definition.profile?.status === 'unknown' (isUnknownInstrumentDefinition) and report instead of {0,127} / 'keys'.

partComposer.ts task table (WOODWINDS / ensemble / INTRO / ENDING / TRANSITION) -> use the resolved profile's gestures (profile.gestures) instead of the fixed figures; 'ensemble' resolves to string_section.

sectionPhrasePlanner.ts / arrangementArc (B-01) -> call shouldRest per window with { sectionFunction, energy, barsIntoSection, soloEntry, vocalActive, isFinalChorus } and the arc's { dynamic, textureLevel, tensionRole, familyEntryBar, requested }; record the RestDecision on the role assignment.

exportEngine.ts ~line 760 (sfizz candidates) -> assessKeyRangeFit(rendered.trackModel.notes, { keyRange: candidate.keyRange }) before renderAttested; refuse with the reason like the pedalboard path does. nativeRendererRouting.ts already types keyRange on SfizzInstrumentMapEntry.
performanceEngine.ts:profileFor -> FAMILY_PROFILES has no 'winds' / 'unknown' row (falls back to keys); add a winds row (breath-phrase) and make unknown explicit.
The lead's local worker (:8022): restart to publish ranges; optionally python annotate_manifest.py to write them into the manifest.
